ai.description: This toad reaches 4–5 cm. It is dark brown with a pale vertebral stripe and granular skin. Key features include a prominent, elongated parotoid gland and a distinct, dark-pigmented throat.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus silentvalleyensis* is best distinguished by its unique, prominent, and continuous cranial ridges that form a distinct "V" shape on the top of its head.
ai.habitat: The South Indian Hill Toad inhabits the evergreen forests of the Silent Valley National Park, typically found at elevations ranging from 800 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The South Indian Hill Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky stream banks of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus silentvalleyensis* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings within shallow, slow-moving water.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus silentvalleyensis* is endemic to the Silent Valley National Park in Kerala’s Western Ghats, occurring at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The South Indian Hill Toad emits a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in the Silent Valley’s evergreen forests.
